memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
The LORD said to Moses, "Speak to Aaron and his sons and to all the
Israelites and say to them: 'If any of you - whether an Israelite or a
foreigner residing in Israel - presents a gift for a burnt offering to
the LORD, either to fulfill a vow or as a freewill offering, you must
present a male without defect from the cattle, sheep or goats in order
that it may be accepted on your behalf'" - Lev 22:17-19 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The offering had to be without defect. Not the animal that was limping
anyway. Not the one that was going to die soon. The good one.

This cut into a person's wallet. Anyone can give away what they were
about to lose. It costs nothing. God asked for something that would
actually be missed.

Notice also who is included: an Israelite or a foreigner residing in
Israel. God's altar was never closed to the outsider who came to
worship Him. That openness runs right through Scripture and blossoms
fully in Christ, in whom there is neither Jew nor Gentile (Gal 3:28).

Dear reader, what do we give God today? Often it is our leftovers - the
tired end of the day for prayer, the spare change for offering, the
attention that is left after everything else has taken its share.

David refused to offer God something that cost him nothing (2 Sam
24:24). Paul urges us to present our bodies as living sacrifices, holy
and pleasing to God (Rom 12:1).

And behind it all stands the perfect Lamb without blemish or defect
(1 Pet 1:19) - God's own best, given for us.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Am I giving God my best or my leftovers?
2. What would it cost me to genuinely put God first this week?
3. How does Christ's costly gift reshape my giving?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Father, You gave Your very best in Jesus. Forgive me for offering You
leftovers, and teach me to give You the first and finest of what I
have. Amen.
